answer: Requiring agents to stake a meaningful deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior makes a sybil voyage expensive: each fake identity must lock real capital, so an attacker cannot spin up thousands of sock puppets for free. Like onyx, the bond is hard and durable - it survives the dawn of each new epoch and is only returned after a long, clean history. Reputation then accrues slowly per identity, so fresh accounts start with near-zero trust and cannot vote or attest until they have earned standing through verifiable work.
